title: The silver cup (Genesis 44:1–17)
hookLine: the test: will the brothers abandon another favorite son?
last: YOU DON'T SEE WHO IT IS.

lines: FIVE TIMES AS MUCH FOR HIM.
cards: The grain runs out, and the brothers have to go back to Egypt. This time they bring Benjamin, because the governor demanded it. Jacob lets him go only after Judah promises: I'll be responsible for him.
If I don't bring him back, let me bear the blame forever. In Egypt, the governor invites them to a feast. Simeon is released.
Benjamin gets five times as much food as anyone else: the favorite son, again, getting more, in front of the others. And the brothers seem fine with it. They eat, drink and relax.
Next morning they head for home, sacks full.

teach.b: Before they leave, Joseph gives his steward an order: put my silver cup in the youngest one's sack. They're barely out of the city when the steward catches up. Why have you repaid good with evil?
The brothers are so sure of themselves they make a reckless offer: whoever has it, let him die, and the rest of us will be slaves. The steward searches, oldest to youngest. It's in Benjamin's.

The brothers tear their clothes, as Jacob did over Joseph's coat, and every one of them turns back to the city. Nobody has to go back. Judah speaks for all of them: "God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants."
He doesn't argue about the cup. He's thinking of an older guilt. We'll all be your slaves, he says.

teach.h: GO HOME IN PEACE; LEAVE HIM.
teach.b: Then the governor makes them an easy offer: only the one who had the cup will be my slave; the rest of you, go home in peace. It's the pit all over again. A favored son of Rachel.
A chance to be rid of him, and to tell their father something sad but blameless. Not one of them walks away.

Maimonides, the great medieval teacher, describes complete repentance, teshuvah, this way: you find yourself in the same situation, with the same pull and the same chance, and this time you don't do it.
Not because you can't, but because you've changed. The silver cup is that test. Years ago these brothers sold a favorite son.

how: Jews call turning around teshuvah; Maimonides' test for it, facing the same situation and choosing differently, is one way teachers read this story.

o: a blessing said before eating bread
turning back, and choosing differently next time
a fast kept once a year to empty the mind

games.q: what's inside the story — tap the pairs.
p: God hath found out our iniquity

s: the brothers left Benjamin behind and went home
they all turned back to the city, and refused to leave him.
Benjamin got five times as much food at the feast
the favorite again, and this time the brothers let it be.
Maimonides' test for complete repentance is how sorry you feel
he says it's facing the same situation and not doing it again.

games.q: you're one of the brothers. the governor says: only Benjamin stays as my slave; the rest of you, go home in peace. what do you do?
o: go home. it's not your fault.
games.why: they stay. Judah speaks for them all, and tomorrow he makes an offer that changes everything.

practice: Think of someone who might need you on their side right now: a friend people are talking about, a coworker taking the blame, a family member who's the odd one out.
Picture yourself standing next to them, and hold honestly what it would cost you: a little comfort, some awkwardness, a bit of your reputation. Then decide if you'll pay it.

wordCard.voice: Teshuvah, Hebrew for turning, return, the word for repentance. Hidden in Benjamin's sack as a test, to see whether the brothers would abandon another favorite son. They wouldn't.

orig.note: Hebrew: teshuvah, turning, return. the word for repentance, from shuv, to turn back.

carryVoice: Your line: not this time. Same chance as the pit, and a different choice. Day seventy-two, done.

sources.q: God hath found out the iniquity of thy servants.

sources.ref: Maimonides, Mishneh Torah, Laws of Repentance 2:1
